citations.quote: For taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025 but before January 1, 2027, any individual or married individuals filing jointly may claim a refundable credit against tax in an amount equal to 20 percent of the credit claimed by the individual or married individuals for federal individual income taxes
citations.source: Code of Virginia § 58.1-339.8 (Income tax credit for low-income taxpayers)

citations.quote: An income tax credit equal to 20% of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit. The credit is refundable, so it can be more than the total amount of your tax.
citations.source: Virginia Tax, Virginia Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) & Credit for Low Income Individuals

summary: Va. Code § 58.1-339.8(3) lets a filer claim a refundable credit for taxable years 2025 and 2026. The credit equals 20% of the federal § 32 EITC and is taken in place of the nonrefundable low-income credit and the nonrefundable EITC. The head is 40 and has no children, so the federal EITC is 7.65% × $520 = $39.78, which gives $7.96 for Virginia. The engine's steps match this, and stage 1 reached the same figure. The consensus answer of $0 rests on the wrong belief that the credit is nonrefundable or has expired. The only open point is rounding: the IRS lookup table gives an EITC of $40, which would make the Virginia credit $8.00.
